message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on a hangtag fastener (a loop-lock fastener made of braided polyester monofilament with plastic pieces). The likely classification is 5609.00, articles of yarn, n.e.s.

Alternatives considered:
- 3926.90 (other articles of plastics) was rejected because the textile string gives the article its essential character.
- 5609.00.30 covers articles of man-made fibers yarn, strip or the like of heading 5404 or 5405, twine, cordage, rope or cables.
- Monofilament of 5404 qualifies, but the fastener has a plastic locking piece.
- The 5609 subheadings are 5609.00.1000 (of cotton), 5609.00.2000 (of fibers of 5404/5405?), 5609.00.3000 (of other man-made fibers), and 5609.00.4000 (other).

I recall the HTSUS 5609.00 breakdown as: 5609.00.10 of cotton; 5609.00.20 of man-made fibers, 5609.00.30? I am not certain. Another version I recall is 5609.00.20 "Of man-made fibers"? and 5609.00.30 "Of other fibers"? Of these, 5609.00.3000 is "Other: Of yarn, strip or the like of heading 5404 or 5405, twine, cordage, rope or cables". 5609.00.4000 is "Other".

Since the item is made of polyester monofilament, I choose 5609.00.4000 as a safer pick. The specific item is an article of monofilament yarn, not twine, cordage or rope. The braided yarn is arguably cordage-like, but it is a fastener. I'll go with 5609.00.4000.

{"hts_code": "5609.00.4000", "reason": "The braided polyester monofilament fastener with molded plastic pin and lock is an article of yarn not elsewhere specified, classified in heading 5609 as an other article."}
